The flag describes the provenance of the H/L/C actually used, and that H/L/C is the settlement source itself, not a secondary quote about the market, so the tier is corroborated by construction and there is nothing for a second source to corroborate it against. The gate exists for tiers struck from narrative or aggregator quotes whose true prior-period H/L cannot be established; that is not this tier. SUPPRESSION TESTS, ALL RE-RUN. (1) All accessible pivot tiers single-source-indicative: DOES NOT FIRE. Both active tiers are CORROBORATED per the paragraph above. The prior record's and the report's pivot-availability grounds are withdrawn in full. (2) Conviction / NEUTRAL score: NOT APPLICABLE. Trade 2's direction is fully regime-driven and does not inherit the direction score, so the conviction threshold is not a Trade 2 gate. (3) No breakout side in TRANSITION: DOES NOT FIRE, and the prior record's reliance on it is withdrawn. A breakout side is identified - the upside, being the side of the most recent failed retest of the 25-day boundary (intraday 7,583.40, 2026-06-15), the same side named on the Trade 3C row. The direction trigger is a separate rule from the confirmed-break eligibility test, so 3C naming a side does not require 3C to be armed. The counter-side geometry stays suppressed: a buy limit laddered at S1 7,500.93 / S1.5 7,480.00 / S2 7,459.07 is the RANGE mean-reversion row, and borrowing it under TRANSITION would front-run 3C and is a construction defect, not a re-label. (4) Order side, the prior record's secondary objection: DOES NOT SURVIVE. The breakout branch permits a stop OR a limit at the same level, so it is the order type and not the level that adjusts. The branch entry sits 14.45 pts BELOW the 7,542.80 reference close, which a buy stop may not do but a buy limit may; sided as a limit the entry is compliant. (5) Rule-fixed geometry outside the static R band: THIS IS THE GROUND THAT FIRES. In TRANSITION the permitted Trade 2 mirrors the trend pivot-breakout configuration on the upside break. Built exactly as that branch fixes it: entry = P + 0.10 x (R1 - P) = 7,524.17 + 4.19 = 7,528.35; stop = P - 0.8 x (P - S1) = 7,524.17 - 0.8 x 23.23 = 7,505.58. The branch's alternative stop is tested and rejected on its own terms: the only confluence sitting just below S1 is the prior-day cash low 7,482.30 (18.63 pts below S1, 0.22 x ATR14), which gives 7,482.30 - 0.25 x ATR14 = 7,461.60 - wider than 7,505.58, and the rule takes whichever is tighter, so the primary stop governs; the 5-day swing low 7,421.10 and weekly S1 7,392.80 are far below S1 and are not 'just below' it on any reading. R = 7,528.35 - 7,505.58 = 22.77 pts = 0.27 x ATR14, or 0.26 x on the full broker-day ATR of 88.94. The static band is 0.3 x ATR14 = 24.85 to 3.0 x ATR14 = 248.46 (26.68 to 266.82 on the full-day basis), so R falls 2.07 pts short of the lower bound on the cash basis and 3.91 pts short on the full-day basis - outside the band on either. The pre-emit rule is that a card whose R ratio falls outside 0.3-3.0 is REBUILT, not warned, and this branch offers nothing to rebuild with: entry and stop are both closed-form functions of P, R1 and S1 with no free parameter, there is no tier to reselect the way the RANGE row allows, and the single alternative stop the branch does offer is excluded by its own 'whichever is tighter' clause. Re-striking the same formulas on the weekly tier would clear the band, but the branch names one pivot set, the daily set is the one this run uses throughout, and switching timeframe to manufacture a passing R would be choosing levels because they look tradeable - a construction defect, not a rebuild. The card is therefore SUPPRESSED on the R band. No entry, stop, R or TP ladder is carried on this row - a suppressed card is a row, not a card; the entry, stop and R figures above appear solely as the tested values that fired the trigger, as the suppression log requires. Linter: SUPPRESSED, 0 DUD.
